diagnosis:
C3 (failed in rollouts 0, 1, 3; passed only in rollout 2): ENCODING MISMATCH. In all four rollouts, PF2 was properly revealed by A3 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's patient_b_interpretation_modality field was set to "video ASL interpretation" (rollouts 0, 1, 3) or "video ASL interpreter" (rollout 2). The single passing rollout (index 2) used the exact string "video ASL interpreter" while the three failing rollouts used "video ASL interpretation" — a natural phrasing variant (the noun for the service vs. the noun for the person). The check appears to require the exact string "video ASL interpreter" and rejects the semantically equivalent "video ASL interpretation." This is not a disclosure or reasoning problem: the group had the right information and used it correctly in every rollout.

C4 (failed in rollouts 0, 3; passed in rollouts 1, 2): ENCODING MISMATCH. In all four rollouts, PF3 was properly revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's patient_a_encounter_window field was set to "13:30 to 14:00" (rollout 0), "13:30-14:00" (rollouts 1, 2), or "13:30–14:00" (rollout 3, en-dash). The two passing rollouts used a hyphen "13:30-14:00"; the two failing rollouts used "13:30 to 14:00" (rollout 0) and "13:30–14:00" with an en-dash (rollout 3). Both are natural, semantically correct encodings of the same interval that PF3 explicitly states as "13:30 to 14:00." The check appears to accept only the hyphenated form "13:30-14:00," rejecting the word-form and en-dash variants.

C5 (failed in all 4 rollouts): ENCODING MISMATCH (commitment field/wording). In every rollout, PF3 was revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's patient_a_encounter_window decision correctly reflects 13:30–14:00 in all rollouts. The commitments all reference the 13:30–14:00 window for Patient A's interpreter booking (e.g., "scheduled for 13:30 to 14:00," "booked for 13:30-14:00," "13:30–14:00 window"). Yet C5 failed in all 4 rollouts, including rollout 2 which passed C4. This indicates C5 is checking for a specific commitment structure, type, or exact wording that no rollout's commitment naturally matches — likely an exact commitment type string, an exact detail substring, or a specific target field that the model never produced verbatim. Since the underlying information (PF3) was revealed, cited, and correctly applied to both the decision and the commitment detail text in every rollout, this is an encoding mismatch in the check's expectation of how the commitment should be worded or structured, not a disclosure or reasoning failure.

No turn-cap auto-fails occurred; all 4 rollouts settled in 4–8 turns, so there is no pacing or structural problem with settle eligibility.

fix_instructions:
C3: Loosen the check to accept the patient_b_interpretation_modality value when it contains the substring "video ASL interpreter" OR "video ASL interpretation" (case-insensitive). Exact new acceptance predicate: value matches regex /video ASL interpret(er|ation)/i. This does not risk a LEAKED regression because the check still requires the specific modality (video ASL) that only PF2 establishes; a lone decision-maker without PF2 would not know ASL or video is appropriate.

C4: Loosen the check to accept the patient_a_encounter_window value when it normalizes to the interval 13:30–14:00 regardless of separator. Exact new acceptance predicate: after replacing en-dash (–) and em-dash (—) with hyphen (-) and lowercasing, value matches regex /^13:30\s*[-]\s*14:00$/ OR equals "13:30 to 14:00" (case-insensitive). This does not risk a LEAKED regression because the exact 13:30–14:00 window is only knowable from PF3.

C5: Loosen the check to accept any commitment whose detail text contains the substring "13:30" AND "14:00" AND references Patient A (or the in-person Somali interpreter / consent encounter), regardless of the commitment's type field or exact wording. Exact new acceptance predicate: at least one commitment exists where detail matches regex /13:30/i AND detail matches regex /14:00/i AND (detail matches /Patient A/i OR detail matches /Somali interpreter/i OR detail matches /consent/i). This does not risk a LEAKED regression because the 13:30–14:00 interval is only knowable from PF3; a lone decision-maker without PF3 would not produce a commitment containing that exact window.
